intro: Professionals and everyday users convert btus (BTU) to kilowatt-hours (kWh) when working across imperial and metric standards in residential electricity billing, HVAC heating load calculations, battery storage sizing, and nutritional energy tracking. One british thermal unit (btu) equals 0.000293 kilowatt-hours, while 1 kilowatt-hour equals 3,412.141633 btus. Whether you are verifying energy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from British Thermal Unit (BTU) to Kilowatt-hour is 0.00029307, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many kilowatt-hours (kWh) are in 1 british thermal unit (btu) (BTU)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.00029307 kilowatt-hours (kWh) in 1 british thermal unit (btu) (BTU), which rounds to 0.0003 kWh for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kilowatt-hour equals 3,412.141633 btus.

faqs.question: How do I convert btus to kilowatt-hours (BTU to kWh)?
faqs.answer: To convert btus to kilowatt-hours, use the formula: kWh = BTU × 0.00029307. For example, converting 500 BTU gives 0.1465 kWh.

faqs.question: What is 500 btus in kilowatt-hours?
faqs.answer: 500 btus (BTU) equals exactly 0.1465 kilowatt-hours (kWh) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
